learning_outcomes.text: Has basic knowledge regarding the generation, transmission and distribution of electrical energy, knows the construction and operating principles of devices used in power engineering.
Knows basic methods, techniques, materials, and technologies used in the design and creation of electrical devices.

Is able to perceive non-technical aspects, including environmental, economic, and legal, when formulating and solving tasks related to the design of elements, circuits, and systems in electrical engineering.
Is able to obtain information from literature, databases, and other sources; is able to integrate acquired information, interpret it, draw conclusions, and formulate and justify opinions.
Is able to prepare documentation for an engineering task and prepare a text containing a discussion of the results of this task.
Is able to apply learned mathematical methods and models, as well as computer techniques, for the analysis and evaluation of electrical engineering elements and circuits.

Is aware of the importance and understands the non-technical aspects and consequences of an electrical engineer's activities, including their impact on the environment, and the associated responsibility for decisions made.
Is aware of the importance of acting professionally, adhering to professional ethics principles, and respecting diversity of views and cultures.

syllabus_topics: Basic concepts used in reliability theory - failure and restoration of devices; causes of failures.
Statistical studies of reliability parameters of electrical power devices and systems.
Reliability parameters of objects without and with restoration.
Methods for determining the reliability of electrical power supply systems.
Improving the quality and reliability of electrical power supply systems.
Cost-effectiveness analysis of improving power supply reliability.
Analysis of power supply unreliability costs.
Optimization of the reliability level of electrical power supply systems.
Determining the reliability of simple systems without and with restoration.
Principles of parametric and non-parametric estimation.
Calculating the reliability level of electrical power supply systems.
Optimization of the system's reliability level.
Analysis of data regarding power grid failures.
teaching_methods: Visual thinking (mind mapping, concept mapping, sketchnoting)
Practice method (doing tasks at the blackboard)
assessment_rules: For lectures, passing the final colloquium on the lecture topics is required. For auditorium classes, active participation in discussions and exercise classes is required, along with presenting the results of network failure data analysis and passing all partial colloquia. The evaluation of student work may be based on oral or written statements in the form of a colloquium, which, in accordance with the AGH study regulations, translates into the final grade for this form of classes.
